item.title: Dr. Wondertainment's Miniatures Paint Wash
item.content:encoded:
This is a great -J in that it was a bit funny, but left me wondering in the same way as a normal SCP (the good thought-provoking ones, anyway). This COULD be a main-list SCP, in that its existence in-setting wouldn't disrupt much of anything, and would kinda fit in. Of course, it was written as a joke, and that's what matters.
Taken seriously, I'm left wondering where the hell this stuff came from. Is it all the black mascara worn by all the teenage boys from 1989 to 2000? Is it a memeto-bacterial infestation commonly found in comic-book presses shortly before the conversion to modern digital systems? I like my post title theory best, but the best-fit for a serious answer might be that it was created by a young and emotionally disturbed reality shifter.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
This joke is up for review. It's pretty dark, so maybe you can shine some light on it?

I feel like the description for this one goes on for too long. It starts to feel like a pretty generic SCP retelling of the "grimdark" trend. The containment procedures and expungement don't work very well as part of the joke, and it doesn't really get funny until the test logs. With all the sludge you have to go through in the description, the test logs end up not being as funny as they would be if the description here were tightened up more.

item.content:encoded:
I figured it would be a bit presumptuous to add an SCP and a lengthy experiment log in one go, because I don't know if the response I got in chat will be reflected in the voting on the wiki proper. I know, it sounds lazy, but since this is my first joke SCP and I'm still new, I figured I'd play it safe.

I wouldn't inherently be adverse to others adding their own experiments; I had a few other ones that I had thought to add, but decided to stick with a few to convey the "liquid Grimdark" feel.
